subject: Provider routing & fallback commitments for cross-border TIA
messages:
From: Daniel Hsu <daniel.hsu@medisecure.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: legalops@medisecure.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Provider routing & fallback commitments for TIA scoping

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. As we scope the Technical Impact Assessment (TIA/DTIA) for our EU workloads, the legal and infra teams have a few focused asks around how Redwood will route EU-origin requests, and what fallback behavior looks like when a preferred region or model variant is unavailable. Specifically:

- Can you confirm whether requests from our EU tenants can be hard-pinned to eu-west-1 and covered by the UK Addendum/SCCs guarantee?
- If routing falls back to a non-EU region (e.g., us-west), what contractual safeguards do you have (contractual SCCs + subprocessors list + encryption in transit at rest)?
- We need a subprocessor roster that includes network CDNs and any cloud infra providers involved in KV cache replication (including roles & access limits).

For the TIA, our security reviewer asked for a matrix mapping: inbound origin -> primary region -> fallback region -> data residency guarantees. Could you share a draft? attaching a simple inventory template we want you to populate (TIA_inventory.xlsx).

Can we aim to have the draft matrix and subprocessors roster by next Wednesday (2027-03-10)? Our procurement/legal teams will use it to validate the UK IDTA addendum clauses.

Thanks,
Daniel Hsu
Head of Security Operations | Medisecure
Daniel.Hsu@medisecure.com

Attachments: TIA_inventory.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Hsu <daniel.hsu@medisecure.com>
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Provider routing & fallback commitments for TIA scoping

Hi Daniel —

Really helpful list, thanks. We can absolutely provide the matrix you describe and populate your inventory template. Quick answers up front:

- EU pinning: yes — for customers on Redwood Private or Dedicated with an EU region selection we can pin inference to eu-west-1 and enforce routing via our smart-router. For Hosted customers we offer regional routing policies; we will document the conditions where hard-pinning is supported vs. best-effort routing (we'll mark those cases in the matrix).

- Fallbacks: when a fallback to a non-EU region occurs, we will:
  1) fall back to a compatible model variant (same or quantized model family)
  2) apply SCCs + UK Addendum (where applicable) and maintain encryption in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest (AES-256)
  3) emit an audit event and customer-visible trace showing the fallback event and the region used

- Subprocessors: we will produce a consolidated roster with roles (e.g., network CDN, observability vendor, cloud infra provider) and whether they have access to plaintext user prompts/outputs or only encrypted buckets/metadata.

Grace — can you take the lead on building the matrix and draft roster? Marissa, please pull the current subprocessor list and highlight any suppliers with EU data processing (especially caching/CDN). Daniel, we'll attach the draft files to this thread shortly.

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Enterprise | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Provider routing & fallback commitments for TIA scoping

Hi all — I'm attaching a first-pass draft of the routing/fallback matrix and a preliminary subprocessor mapping. Notes:

- Matrix (see attachment: TIA_network_map_v1.pdf): we model three origin buckets: EU web UI, EU API tokens (server-to-server), and queued batch jobs. For Hosted customers, EU routing is policy-based; for Dedicated/Private we can enforce hard pinning.

- Fallback behavior: priority order is (1) same-region compatible variant, (2) region-bound compatible variant with contractual SCCs & UK Addendum, (3) last-resort partner edge (only metadata allowed). We include the audit-event fields that will be surfaced in the Console (route_reason, fallback_region, model_variant_used).

- Subprocessor roster (see provider_fallback_matrix.csv): lists CDNPartner (edge caching, no plaintext access), CloudInfraCo (GPU fleet, limited KV-access for cache replication — encrypted in transit), ObservabilityCorp (metrics only, anonymized).

Open items we still need from you, Daniel:
1) Confirmation whether Medisecure requires an explicit contractual guarantee that no fallback to non-EU occurs (some customers require this as a DPA addendum clause).
2) Any additional compliance evidence format you prefer (SOC 2 report snippet, subprocessor attestations, or three formal references).

I'll also add a column to the matrix indicating which items are demonstrable via logs vs contractual controls.

- Grace O'Connor
Product Security Manager | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com

Vanessa / Grace —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the draft attachments. A few follow-ups from legal:

- We don't require a blanket prohibition on non-EU fallbacks, but we do require: (a) that fallbacks to non-EU regions be logged with customer-visible alerts, and (b) that fallback routes be covered by SCCs and the UK Addendum. Your proposed audit fields and the contractual commitment above will satisfy that.

- For the subprocessor roster, legal needs the following fields: company name, country of operations, roles (access to plaintext yes/no), and date of most recent audit or attestation. If you can add those to the CSV, we're close.

- Last ask: can Redwood provide a short statement we can append to our UK IDTA addendum confirming that: "Redwood Inference applies SCCs to cross-border fallbacks and will notify the customer when such a fallback occurs." A one-paragraph confirmation signed by your legal or compliance lead would be great.

If you can ship the updated matrix + enhanced roster and the legal statement by EOD Monday (2027-03-08), procurement will begin the DPA addendum review.

Thanks —
Daniel
Head of Security Operations | Medisecure
